## What the tutorial covers

The afternoon opens with a short [intro](presentation/00-intro/), then four parts in two sessions. Part descriptions from the [ALTA 2026 program](https://alta2026.alta.asn.au/program#afternoon-tutorial):

**Session 1: Foundations of AI Agent Evaluation**

1. **AI Agents and Evaluation Challenges** (Terrence Szymanski) — agents, tool use, and why final-answer scoring is not enough.
2. **LLM-as-a-Judge Methods** (Parvin Zarei Eskikand) — criteria, rubrics, scales, prompts, and the trade-offs with rules and human review.

**Session 2: Practical Evaluation of AI Agents**

3. **Hands-on Agent Evaluation Exercise** (Yelaman Abdullin) — build a rubric and a judge, then look at tool choice, parameters, and response quality.
4. **Reliability, Limitations, and Future Directions** (Sara Mirabi) — consistency, cost, failure modes, and open research.

Presenters: Parvin Zarei Eskikand (SEEK), Terrence Szymanski (SEEK), Sara Mirabi (Deakin University), and Yelaman Abdullin (Macquarie University).

Participants should bring a laptop. Basic familiarity with machine learning, NLP, and large language models is enough. LLM access for the exercise will be confirmed before the tutorial.
